result.rationale: The diff shows parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse envelope (`return refreshTokenResponse;`, not `.data`), and in googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the result is stored directly: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); await prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Previously it was `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`. So the credential key becomes `{success, data, error}` instead of parsed credentials, breaking subsequent refreshes/usage. Mechanism fully verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: Google Calendar credential is corrupted by the safeParse envelope: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~96-99) returns the Zod `{ success, data, error }` envelope which is stored directly as `credential.key` instead of the parsed data, so after the first token refresh every subsequent refresh and calendar operation fails until the user manually re-auths — data loss on the default path for all Google Calendar integrations

adjudication.rationale: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full Zod safeParse result (the `{ success, data, error }` envelope) rather than the parsed `data` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, it `return refreshTokenResponse;`). In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff changes from `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (returns parsed data) to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists `key` directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That would store the envelope object as `credential.key`, corrupting the expected credential shape for subsequent operations.
